decisions.reason: As a flagship product close to the core business and still promoted on the home page, it likely meets aspiration levels well enough that an expanding firm has little reason to withdraw it.
This software builds on the established oncology QA offering and its continued standalone presentation suggests acceptable performance, so boundedly rational management would likely retain it.
Because it is a new but closely related extension of the firm's imaging QA activities, the firm's growth and product breadth provide enough slack to keep it while results are still emerging.

Although this mammography phantom is more distant from the historical core, the firm's expansion and strategic move into imaging QA make retention more likely unless early sales fall clearly below aspiration.
This is another more distant mammography product and therefore faces a higher risk of review, but the firm's slack and broader imaging QA push still make keeping it the more likely choice in 2025.
As a flagship 2024 product line that fits the stated direction toward integrated imaging QA, it is unlikely to be dropped so soon by a growing innovative firm.
